section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that lower fear is considered a small matter relative to Moshe's level of higher knowledge, yet it is specifically this lower fear that God demands because it brings about the ultimate delight through the nullification of the yesh.
section.t: And to understand more deeply that the souls of Israel are in the aspect of pnimiyus (innerness),
it is written,
"And now, Israel, what does Hashem your G-d ask of you, but to fear [Him]..."
And our sages, of blessed memory, said,
"Is fear then such a small matter?"
"Yes, relative to Moshe it is a small matter."
And behold,
what is said, "but to fear,"
refers to the lower fear,
for this is what is meant by "but to fear,"
that is, it is the most inferior level of fear,
and therefore relative to Moshe it is a small matter.
And the explanation of this is,
for it is written,
"For a G-d of knowledge is Hashem,"
[meaning] two types of knowledge,
higher knowledge and lower knowledge.
Higher knowledge is that above there is [true] existence and below there is none,
that is,
one sees with tangible vision that above is the true existence and below is nothing,
and lower knowledge is that creation is yesh me'ayin (existence from nothingness),
that is, below there is existence and above there is none,
since he sees only the created existence,
therefore he calls what is below "existence" and what is above "nothingness."
And according to the difference between these two types of knowledge, there is also a difference in their bittul (self-nullification),
that the bittul stemming from lower knowledge is only the nullification of the yesh (the sense of self-existence),
for since he sees the yesh,
he is in a state of existence,
except that nevertheless he also has a matter of bittul,
the nullification of the yesh,
but the bittul stemming from higher knowledge is a bittul bimetzius (nullification of [one's very] existence),
for since he sees that below is nothing,
therefore the bittul is a nullification of existence.
And this is that relative to Moshe, lower fear is a small matter,
for behold, Moshe is in the aspect of higher knowledge,
as our sages, of blessed memory, said,
"All the prophets prophesied through 'koh' (thus), but Moshe prophesied through 'zeh' (this),"
for "zeh" is the vision of the essence,
the aspect of higher knowledge,
by virtue of which he was in the state of bittul bimetzius,
and therefore relative to Moshe, who is in the aspect of higher knowledge,
bittul bimetzius,
behold, lower fear, which is only in the aspect of nullification of the yesh,
is a small matter.
And behold,
even though lower fear is a lowly level,
a small matter,
about which it was said "but to fear,"
nevertheless,
it is demanded
(one demands)
specifically lower fear,
because the ultimate intention and primary delight is in lower fear more than in higher fear,
as it is written,
"Laughter has G-d made for me,"
that specifically through effecting the matter of bittul in the things that come from the name Elokim, which are in the aspect of yesh,
the nullification of the yesh to the ayin,
then the primary matter of laughter and delight is brought about Above,
and likewise it is written,
"The Leviathan, which You formed to sport with it,"
for Leviathan is from the term connection,
as it is written,
"My husband will be joined to me,"
and the matter of connection applies specifically when there are two distinct things separate from each other,
and this matter is specifically in the service of nullification of the yesh,
for the yesh and the ayin are two distinct things separate from each other,
and nevertheless one effects the nullification of the yesh to the ayin,
and through this specifically the matter of laughter is brought about,
"to sport with it."
And this is,
that although the service of is'hapcha (transformation) is higher than the service of is'kafya (subjugation),
this is only regarding the matter of revelations,
but the primary delight is specifically in the service of is'kafya.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that every Jewish soul contains a spark of Moshe, the aspect of Mah (bittul bimetzius), and the hundred blessings are instituted to reveal this Mah within the soul.
section.t: However, we still need to understand what is said, "relative to Moshe it is a small matter,"
for at first glance it is not understood,
after all, it is written "from you" (i.e., it is asked of every Jew).
But the explanation is,
as explained in Tanya,
that every single soul of the house of Israel has within it from the aspect of Moshe Rabbeinu,
a spark from the soul of Moshe,
and it is the aspect of Mah (What) that is in every Jew,
which is the matter of bittul bimetzius
(as above),
and this is because the root of the souls is from the aspect of Chochmah (Wisdom),
as it is written,
"You are children to Hashem your G-d,"
and it is written,
"My firstborn son is Israel,"
and just as a son is drawn from the very essence of his father's brain,
so too, the souls are from the very essence of the aspect of Chochmah,
which is the aspect of Mah.
And therefore the souls are in a state of ultimate bittul,
bittul bimetzius,
as it is written,
"As Hashem, the G-d of Israel, lives, before Whom I stand,"
which refers to all souls,
that they are in a manner of standing,
which is the matter of bittul.
And this is, "And now, Israel, what (Mah) does Hashem your G-d ask of you, but to fear,"
since all of Israel are in the aspect of Mah,
from the spark of Moshe that is in every Jew,
behold, "what does Hashem your G-d ask of you, but to fear,"
that fear is a small matter relative to the spark of Moshe that is in every Jew.
And in order to reveal the aspect of Mah in the soul,
behold, for this they instituted one hundred blessings,
as our sages, of blessed memory, said,
"Do not read 'Mah' (what) but 'Me'ah' (one hundred),"
from which they learned that a person is obligated to bless one hundred blessings every day,
for one hundred blessings is in the manner of what is written,
"And Yitzchak sowed in that land and found... one hundred gates, and Hashem blessed him,"
and this is,
that through the service of tzedakah (charity/righteousness),
"sows acts of righteousness,"
the blessing and drawing down from Above is effected, so that the aspect of Mah in the soul is revealed.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that in exile, the service is only in externality, so we ask "Remember, Hashem, what has befallen us" to recall the concealed Mah, and we request "look" (habatah) which is a distant, encompassing revelation that blinds the external forces.
section.t: However, in the time of exile, the service is not in the aspect of Mah, which is the pnimiyus (innerness) of the soul,
but only in the aspect of externality and the hind-part (achorayim) alone,
therefore, Above as well, there is "I will surely hide My face"
(as above),
and therefore we ask, "Remember, Hashem, what has befallen us,"
what has become of our Mah,
that the Mah is in concealment and hiding.
And even though it is in concealment,
nevertheless, the matter of remembrance applies,
for ultimately, the essence, root, and very core of the soul is in the aspect of Mah.
And the verse continues, "look (habatah) and see,"
for behold,
the difference between seeing (re'iyah) and looking (habatah) is
that seeing is from close proximity,
as it is written,
"and he saw that he could not prevail against him,"
and looking is from a distance,
as it is written,
"Look from heaven and see,"
and therefore,
the matter of seeing from close proximity cannot be in the time of exile,
and for this we ask for "looking,"
which is the revelation in the aspect of makif (encompassing),
and even though it is in the aspect of makif,
nevertheless, it effects also in the pnimiyus (innerness),
and especially regarding the effect on the kelipot (husks of impurity),
for the encompassing light blinds the eyes of the external forces.
